newsitem.title: FRANCE: Snecma ready to build new jet engines with GE.
newsitem.headline: Snecma ready to build new jet engines with GE.

text.p: French aero-engine maker Snecma is ready to build a more powerful version of the GE90 jet engine with joint venture partner U.S. General Electric as well as a new engine for derivatives of the Airbus A340 long-range plane, Snecma chairman Jean-Paul Bechat said on Monday.

The new engine, currently known as the GEXX, would deliver 55,000-60,000 pounds of thrust and power the A340-500 and 600 Airbus jets, he told journalists. That is double the average output of the CFM56 family of engines Snecma builds with GE.

Bechat said a 20-25 percent share of the GEXX development costs would be consistent with Snecma's resources, estimating a new engine programme would cost about $10 billion while a derivative version could be half that.
A Snecma official said the GEXX would likely be a new engine programme rather than a derivative of a current model.
There are no obstacles to building the GEXX but no decision has been taken yet, Bechat said.

Snecma also wants to develop the GE90 to deliver 100,000 pounds, Bechat said. The previous chairman, Bernard Dufour, was reported last year as being prepared to drop the GE90 development. The engine powers the Boeing 777 twinjet.
A launch decision could be made in 1997 if conditions were right, a SNECMA spokeswoman later said.
Other new products Snecma will work on this year include the CFM56-9 which would power the Asian Express 100 jet being planned by Airbus, China and Singapore Technologies Aerospace.
It will also work on the SPW14 with United Technologies Corp's Pratt & Whitney, which will power the 70-seater jet planned by European consortium Aero International (Regional).
Snecma also hopes to build the M138, which would use the engine core of the M88 engine for a turboprop for the planned Future Large Aircraft (FLA) military transporter.
The company expects to virtually double annual output to 800 CFM56 motors by the end of 1998 from about 400 in 1995, Bechat said.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
